title: Continuous Optimization for p-adic Models
claim: A totally disconnected space becomes path-connected when embedded in a tree-like hull, enabling continuous movement between its points.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right, leader-line labels on points and tree vertices
description: Two panels. Panel (a) shows the 3-adic numbers Q_3 as isolated blue dots grouped into nested triangular clusters, with three separate cluster groups arranged in a triangle. Labeled points include 0, 27, 9, 28, 1, 2 and 29, with gray leader lines marking which dots are near each other under the p-adic metric. Panel (b) shows the p-adic convex hull Γ_3 as a branching gray tree. The same blue dots sit at its leaves inside a shaded pale-blue triangle. Italic labels with arrows mark vertices such as ζ_{0,1}, ζ_{0,1/9}, ζ_{0,1/27} and ζ_{1,1/27}. They also mark edges, with the condition r not in p^Z, and leaves in Q_3 with r=0. The eye goes first to the scattered blue dots on the left, then to the connected tree on the right. Captions under each panel name the space.
caption: The \(3\)-adics are disconnected (left), but path-connected in the \(p\)-adic hull within the Berkovich affine line (right). Not shown are the infinite set of vertices \(\zeta_{x, p^{-v}}\) from a leaf to e.g. \(\zeta_{0,1}\).
abstract: We present the first method for native, continuous gradient descent for machine learning models with $p$-adic parameters. Existing native optimizers are discrete, mostly combinatorial searches, as the $p$-adic numbers $\mathbb{Q}_p$ are totally disconnected, with standard losses that are flat away from their minima. To enable continuous optimization, we propose working with $\mathbb{Q}_p$ via its Berkovich affine line: a canonical, path-connected expansion of $\mathbb{Q}_p$ that preserves its isometries and uniquely extends its analytic maps. This hull is a metric tree with interpretable points and local derivatives, which we show enables effective optimizers and backpropagation. We formulate gradient descent and show that its approximations efficiently learn linear models with coefficients in $\mathbb{Q}_p$ to do modular arithmetic, an XOR-like task not expressible by linear models in $\mathbb{R}$. We also demonstrate momentum and Adam variants, linear regression, and classification on binary-encoded hierarchies (Quillian semantic networks), addressing open problems posed by Martins (2025). Library at https://github.com/google-deepmind/padic-ml
